chunks: Hammād narrated from Ḥurayz, from Zurārah, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said:
The angel does not write down except that which he hears.
Allah, to Whom belong might and majesty, said: Remember your Lord inwardly, in humility and awe…
He said: No one knows the reward of that remembrance within the heart of the servant other than Allah, the Exalted.

key_terms.وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ فِي نَفْسِكَ: Remember your Lord in your self/heart

ai.seo_question: Do angels record inward remembrance (dhikr) in the heart?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqas (AS) clarifies the limitation of the recording angels, who only transcribe audible or declared actions, thereby highlighting the spiritual value of silent, internal dhikr. Citing Quran 7:205, the hadith emphasizes that while angels record outward deeds, the profound reward for private devotion remains exclusively known to Allah, a concept central to Shia understanding of hidden piety (khufya). This distinction underscores the importance of sincerity (ikhlas) in worship, where the heart's connection to God transcends the physical record of deeds.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 4.Ḥammād narrated from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from one of the two (al-Bāqir or al-Ṣādiq) (a) who said, “
The angel does not write down except that which he hears.
Allah, to Whom belong might and majesty, said: Remember your Lord inwardly, in humility and awe… (Q7:205).
Indeed, no one knows the reward of that remembrance within the heart of a servant other than Allah, the Exalted.”
